text:
Aisha Patel: Quick ping — PR #789 (console observability samples) landed but QA flagged that our KV prefetch example is misleading for cost/latency. Can someone take the sample ownership?

Marco Ruiz: I can pick this up. Which part is misleading?

Aisha Patel: The example shows prefetch always reduces cost; in reality it trades off latency vs token cost for different traffic patterns. QA wants a short paragraph + a runtime example showing both win/lose cases.

Sasha Li: Noted. I can add a small section with two mini-playbacks: one high-qps scenario (prefetch on) and one low-qps (prefetch off). Also will add the metric slices we should surface: tokens_per_request, avg_latency_ms, fetch_hit_rate.

Eli: Thx. Can you also add a tiny code snippet for the SDK config? Something like:

```
# python
client = RedwoodClient()
route = client.routes.get('embed-heatmap')
route.configure(prefetch_kv=True, prefetch_window=256)
```

Marco Ruiz: Looks good. Please include expected numbers (order of magnitude) so docs readers know what to look for during smoke testing. e.g., high-qps: latency stable, tokens/token-cost down ~15-30%; low-qps: latency slightly up, cost same or worse.

Sasha Li: Will add a tiny table and a short paragraph explaining tradeoffs + guidance: "enable prefetch for sustained QPS > 10 rps per route; disable for bursty < 2 rps". Will call out that these are heuristics.

Aisha Patel: Also we found 3 broken links in the PR: two that pointed to old tracehook examples and one to an interneal google doc. Please replace with our examples repo links and remove the internal doc.

Eli: I can run a quick link-checker script and paste results here.

docs-bot: Link check finished: 3 failures found — 2 external, 1 internal.

Eli: Pasting output: /docs/tracehook/examples/python -> 404, /internal/kb/kv-prefetch -> permission denied, /examples/old-playback -> 301 redirect.

Marco Ruiz: For the 301, update to canonical example path under examples.redwood.dev. For the internal KB, replace with the public engineering blog post that explains prefetch concepts.

Sasha Li: Will update links and add a short note about measuring cost using the Console cost breakdown panel (linking to the cost/latency dashboard sample). Also will include a caution to pin model versions when comparing numbers.

Aisha Patel: ETA? We want this merged before the docs cut tomorrow morning.

Sasha Li: I can push changes in ~3 hours. I'll ping when ready for review.

Marco Ruiz: I'll review and run a quick smoke test against staging. If timing is tight, I can approve non-blocking fixes after the cut and follow up.

Eli: Once Sasha posts the PR update I’ll re-run link-check + a tiny script to collect cost/latency deltas from staging.

Aisha Patel: Awesome — thanks everyone. Please @channel the PR URL when it's up so QA can re-run their checks. :thumbsup:
